This installer has not yet run on any device. Every device step is unverified until lab test Q-INST-06 is certified.

Device: model srx4100, release 25.2R1-S1.4, serial FIXTURE-SN-4100

LAB ONLY. 'set system scripts language python3' is already set on this device; this install relies on it. It lets any unsigned Python script owned by a super-user-class account run on this device's routing engine, not only J-Wicket: a change to the device's security posture that someone made before. J-Wicket is not qualified for production (gate G1 has not passed). Continue only on a disposable lab device you are allowed to change.
LAB ONLY. With --access tls the runtime commit opens a new HTTPS listener on this device's management address: the --listen-address, by default --host, which the installer does not check is the management address (an address of a revenue interface would put the listener there; in the mgmt_junos routing instance when 'system management-instance' is set). It is reachable by anything that reaches that address: J-Wicket's sign-in page becomes one more way into this device, beside SSH and NETCONF. Its certificate is self-signed; compare its SHA-256 fingerprint in the browser with the one the installer prints. J-Wicket has not passed gate G1 or a security review (Q-SEC-01). Continue only on a lab device whose management network you control.
--lab-hardware: this device is not a vSRX ('show version' reports its model). J-Wicket has run on one lab SRX4100 by hand (docs/deploy-lab.md); this installer has run on no hardware, and the hardware procedure of governance decision D12 is not written: the lab owner decides. The production signs below are what a production firewall would show. After the host name, the installer asks you to type 'lab only'.
Outbound-SSH clients are configured ('show configuration system services outbound-ssh'), so a central manager probably manages this device. This change is made on the box, out of band to the manager, which may report it or overwrite it.
The netconf backend's reach to the device's own NETCONF ('show configuration system services netconf') rests on the probe (check C3) only: it is not checked end to end, because no check uses an SSH channel (SSH forwarding was refused on the lab SRX4100). Sign in once to prove it.

Already present and kept (never removed by this tool):
  set system scripts language python3

The runtime commit starts J-Wicket, listening with TLS on 192.0.2.10:9443 in routing instance mgmt_junos: browse to https://192.0.2.10:9443/ and compare the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint with the one the installer prints.

Blast radius: posture: language python3 already set; listener: HTTPS on 192.0.2.10:9443 in routing instance mgmt_junos, reachable by anything that reaches that address; NETCONF: netconf ssh already set or not needed; account: J-Wicket will run with the rights of labadmin, a super-user-class account that can commit configuration ('username labadmin' under 'system extensions extension-service application file jwicket.py'). A compromise of J-Wicket is a compromise of this device.
Confirm windows: diagnostics 5 min, runtime 5 min
